gallery.title: File:Schooner Zodiac 01.jpg
gallery.description: The two-masted schooner Zodiac, built 1924, was the last working pilot schooner in the United States. Now owned by the Northwest Schooner Society, this picture shows it motoring east along the Lake Washington Ship Canal, just east of the Ballard Bridge (from which this picture was taken), Seattle, Washington, USA. The Zodiac is listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP), ID #82004248.
categories: Ballard Interbay North Manufacturing Industrial Center

gallery.title: File:Aerial view of Ballard, Seattle.jpg
gallery.description: View of Ballard coast with various docks and marinas on Puget Sound/Shilshole Bay, facing north north west. Area near coast is Sunset Hill. The waterway at the bottom is the Lake Washington Ship Canal. On the protruding land in the top center is Golden Gardens Park. Taken by myself from a commercial airliner window.

gallery.filename: Aerial view of Discovery Park and Fort Lawton in Seattle.jpg
gallery.title: File:Aerial view of Discovery Park and Fort Lawton in Seattle.jpg
gallery.description: Aerial view of Magnolia peninsular neighborhood in Seattle, facing north north west. Left is Puget Sound, center right is Lake Washington Ship Canal, top right is Ballard. Bottom left (on the pointy bit) is LH and Sewer Plant, forested area is Discovery Park, brown area is Fort Lawton Military Reserve. Taken by myself from a commercial airliner window.

gallery.filename: Seattle - Portage Bay from E Shelby & 10th E.jpg
gallery.title: File:Seattle - Portage Bay from E Shelby & 10th E.jpg
gallery.description: View of Portage Bay from the corner of E. Shelby St. and 10th Ave E. near the north end of Capitol Hill, Seattle, Washington. Portage Bay, then the Montlake Cut and Montlake Bridge (beyond which Lake Washington and Bellevue). In relative foreground, you can see floating homes at the foot of Shelby.

gallery.filename: Seattle - Portage Bay from E Shelby & 10th E pano.jpg
gallery.title: File:Seattle - Portage Bay from E Shelby & 10th E pano.jpg
gallery.description:
Panoramic view of Portage Bay from just below the corner of E. Shelby St. and 10th Ave E. near the north end of Capitol Hill, Seattle, Washington. 
Portage Bay running across, then the Montlake Cut and Montlake Bridge (beyond which Lake Washington and Bellevue). Across Portage Bay: University of Washington South Campus and Husky Stadium, Montlake.

 This  image was created with Hugin.
Stitched from 5 photos.

gallery.filename: Seattle pano east from Ballard Bridge 01.jpg
gallery.title: File:Seattle pano east from Ballard Bridge 01.jpg
gallery.description: Looking roughly east from Ballard Bridge, Seattle, Washington toward the easternmost part of Salmon Bay. At left, Seattle Maritime Academy (part of Seattle Central Community College) on the north shore of the bay. In the distance, the Fremont Cut of the Lake Washington Ship Canal and the Aurora Bridge.

gallery.filename: Seattle 1909 harbor improvements proposal on topo.jpg
gallery.title: File:Seattle 1909 harbor improvements proposal on topo.jpg
gallery.description: Topographical map of Seattle, Washington, 1909, showing the projected rerouting of the Duwamish River, route for the Lake Washington Ship Canal, and other shoreline proposals. This is more or less what was done (although, for example, more oxbows of the Duwamish were filled in, and not as much change was made to Lake Washington.) Original caption: "Seattle Harbor after the completion of The Lake Washington Ship Canal and Duwamish River Improvement". Compare File:Seattle topo map showing old route of Duwamish River.jpg

gallery.description: Scope and content:  The US Army Corps of Engineers extensively photographed many of the Civil Works project and river and harbor improvement that they were involved with. The Lake Washington Ship Canal and the Hiram Chittenden Locks were built to allow passage between fresh water Lake Union and salt water Puget Sound.
